pass_a_gloss: [...] washing away of sin, that clearly through faith in Christ, where there is supply and grace of the Holy Spirit, and honour of adoption, and enjoyment of unending goods, and hope of kingdom of heavens, there surely is also the need to rejoice, and pain, grief and groaning ran away. For what sort of place will pain have, and over what would groaning come to be, where there is wholly no pretext for groaning and being pained, but rather hope rules, of exultation and gladness, and of delight that cannot be cast off, and of joy? [Lemma, Isaiah 51:12-14:] I am, I am the one comforting you. Know what being you feared from a mortal man, and from a son of man, who withered like grass. And you forgot the God who made you, the one who made the heaven and founded the earth. And you were always fearing all the days the face of the one afflicting you. For in what manner he planned to take you away, and now where is the wrath of the one afflicting you? For in your being saved he will not stand, nor delay. The 'I am' he says in these instead of 'I live and exist'; for indeed he himself is the One Who Is. And this dignity is befitting God and extraordinary; for to be and to live is present only to the nature beyond all, not having obtained these by participation from another, nor having the thing given, but rather being itself the life. So, I am, he says, the one comforting you, that is, the one giving every spiritual comfort, and holding up with helps toward being well set firm, toward the need to go with good courage straight to every virtue. Or perhaps you will understand comfort in these in another way too. For the Saviour was calling through the gospel proclamations to the washing away of sin, that, I say, through faith in him, to sharing of Holy Spirit, and boast and glory of adoption. But you, he says, O Israel, did not fear me who am, overlooking, and despising the one calling to life, but you feared from a corruptible man, and from a son of man, who withered like grass. Then you forgot the God who made you, the one who crafted the heaven, and founded the earth, and you feared the face of the one afflicting you. And God accuses in these the leaders of the Jews, who continued to the end rising against the glory of the Saviour, and as far as it came to them, showing it to be wholly nothing. He worked wonders in many ways; but they poured down beyond wonder bitter words on [his] divine signs; for they were saying that by Beelzebul, ruler of the demons, he casts out the demons. With teachings beyond the law he often charmed those who heard; but they slid down to this [degree] of impiety, so that on those who praised [him] [the section breaks off].
pass_b_english: … washing away of sin, that is, the washing that comes through faith in Christ. Where there is the supply and grace of the Holy Spirit, the honor of adoption, the enjoyment of unending good things, and the hope of the kingdom of heaven, there surely we must rejoice, and pain, grief, and groaning have fled away (Isaiah 51:11). For what place will pain have, and over what could there be groaning, where there is no cause at all for groaning and pain, but rather hope prevails, hope of exultation and gladness, of delight that cannot be lost, and of joy?

“I am, I am he who comforts you. Know who you are, that you were afraid of a mortal man and of a son of man, who have withered like grass. And you forgot God who made you, who made heaven and founded the earth, and you were always afraid, all the days, of the face of him who afflicts you. For just as he planned to take you away, so now where is the fury of him who afflicts you? For in your being saved he will not stop, nor will he delay” (Isaiah 51:12-14).

Here “I am” means “I live and exist”; for he himself is He Who Is (Exodus 3:14). This is a title fitting for God and surpassing all others. For being and living belong only to the nature that is beyond all things, which did not receive them from another by participation, nor holds them as a gift, but rather is itself life.

So he says, “I am he who comforts you,” that is, he who gives every spiritual comfort, and holds you up with his help so that you stand firmly fixed, ready to go with courage straight toward every virtue. Or perhaps you will understand the comfort here in another way too. For through the Gospel proclamations the Savior was calling people to the washing away of sin through faith in him, I mean, to a share in the Holy Spirit, and to the boast and glory of adoption.

But you, O Israel, he says, did not stand in awe of me, who am, but looked down on me and despised him who calls you to life; yet you were afraid of a perishable man and of a son of man, who have withered like grass. Then you forgot God who made you, who fashioned heaven and established the earth, and you feared the face of him who afflicts you.

Here God accuses the leaders of the Jews, who persisted to the end in opposing the Savior's glory, and, as far as it lay with them, declared it to be nothing at all. He worked wonders in many ways, but they poured out astonishingly bitter words on his divine signs; for they said that he cast out demons by Beelzebul, the ruler of the demons (Matthew 12:24). choices.english: I am, I am he who comforts you
choices.why: Isaiah 51:12 is God's word of comfort, not a moral exhortation.
rejected: We must recognize our true nature

choices.why: Exodus 3:14 Septuagint; Cyril explains 'I am' as 'I live and exist'.
God alone has being and life of himself, not by sharing from another.
κατακηλέω, to enchant; his teaching held the hearers.
